q_q_adoption_justification:
I like generation of top-level classes more as they don’t need as much detail. Over all concept should be hard to grasp by GenAI, however there is major gap between how an expert makes design choices and how GenAI creates a rough starting point.
Modeling properties is hard for GenAI, depending on the underlying concepts.
Documentation is not thorough.
Some Classes were created that are not part of AISHIP and are a bit out of intended scope (ClassificationSociety)
Some classes can be reused with minor phrasing corrections.
I prefer starting from scratch
q_q_missing_elements: almost everything. only basic classes are available that still need adaptation.

q_q_adoption_justification:
Good that no properties were created, as this is a complex task.
Some Classes are weird (e. g. GermanFlag). This is on a hierachical level that does not make sense. Components like GPSAntenna also misses the intent of the ontology.
Most other classes hit the scope better, athough by far not perfect. Reuse of existing ontologies/patterns is missing and makes reuse harder.
Overall the maritime concept covered by AISHIP is not so hard to grasp by a GenAI model (in my opinion, unlike e.g., MQTT)
q_q_missing_elements: it just represents a very small fraction of what AISHIP represents. only one of the main 4 modules were hit, with a coverage of about 5 %.

q_q_adoption_justification:
Again, modeling properties should be avoided as it leads to inconsistency in hierarchical structures.
Some classes may better be litterals.
Property naming is weird (e.g., "hasDatabase" connecting Access and Database)

Again, i like no object properties better.
Class naming off. One would not name the class simply "Violated", based on the label.
Documentation is just the class name in a short sentence. no further explanation.
gives the author maybe a better idea of what classes are needed, especially when diving into data access, actions, user rights, etc. But its not very detailed and only covers minor parts.
q_q_additional_observations: Dives a bit more deeply into the CQs. Hits certain keywords mentioned in the CQs and models them as classes. however it majorly depends on the context whether these key words can be directly modeled as classes.
